research_question: Can the divine simplicity theorist consistently maintain that every divine attribute is strictly identical to the divine essence while also affirming a genuine plurality of attributes individuated by sense, role, or account?

argument.title: Reductio against divine simplicity
argument.paper_title: Plantinga and Ash‘arites on Divine Simplicity

premises.text: If divine simplicity is true, then every divine attribute is identical to the divine essence, making all attributes identical with each other.
premises.quote: First, if divine simplicity is accepted, then all the divine attributes would be identical with divine essence, and thus divine attributes would be identical to each other.

premises.text: Consequently, there would be only one divine attribute if all attributes are identical.
premises.quote: That is to say, there would be only one attribute if they are identical.

premises.text: The claim that all attributes are identical is hard to accept because divine attributes like omnipotence, omniscience, and omnibenevolence are multiple.
premises.quote: However, this result is not easy to accept given the multiplicity of divine attributes such as omnipotence, omniscience, and omnibenevolence.

premises.text: Divine simplicity also implies that God is not a personal creator but an abstract object, since properties are abstract objects.
premises.quote: Second, via similar reasoning, it can be shown that God is not a personal being who created the universe but an abstract object since properties are abstract objects.

missing_premise.text: If divine simplicity is false, it must be rejected.

conclusion.text: If these absurd consequences are unacceptable, the doctrine of divine simplicity must be rejected.

challenged_premise.text: Consequently, there would be only one divine attribute if all attributes are identical.

objection: In the video game Apex, the final boss's hit points, attack power, and speed are all coded as the exact same integer, 999, and are not distinct variables—each attribute just is that core value. On the stat screen, however, players see three separate bars labeled HP, ATK, and SPD. The designers do not call this one attribute; they treat it as three distinct attributes that share one identical ground. The players plan around three different abilities. Therefore, even when attributes are strictly identical in their underlying reality, it does not follow that there is only one attribute.

strongest_responses.response: The Apex case is a fair counterexample to a naive inference from identity of ground to identity of attribute-count, but it does not establish that c004 is false as stated because the analogy does not preserve the feature that matters: in the game, HP, ATK, and SPD are distinct at the level of presentation and function, showing that many predicates can share one ground without collapsing into one predicate. The objection therefore shows that the count of attributes depends on individuation, and c004 is vulnerable because it lacks an individuation premise.
strongest_responses.why_it_failed: Defender A conceded that c004 as stated does not survive the objection, since the inference from identity to a single attribute requires an individuation premise that the argument does not supply, though Defender A suggested the objection may not reach the broader worries in c005 and c006 if attributes are distinct only by sense.

strongest_responses.response: The Apex boss has three genuinely distinct attributes—hit points, attack power, and speed—each with a different account, meaning, and scope, so they are not strictly identical; the analogy thus illustrates distinct attributes grounded in one value rather than showing that strict identity permits plurality.
strongest_responses.why_it_failed: The objector replied that if difference in meaning is sufficient to underwrite plurality in the game, the divine simplicity theorist may invoke the same distinction for divine attributes, and if it is insufficient, the analogy survives; Defender B conceded that this exposes a genuine gap and that c004 smuggles in an undefended assumption that ontological identity precludes conceptual distinction.

open_questions: If divine attributes are individuated only by sense or predicative role, does the objection from multiplicity in c005 and the abstractness worry in c006 retain any independent force?

Can the critic independently motivate the revised bridge premise that ontological oneness precludes any difference in meaning, account, or scope without begging the question against the Ash'arite distinction between ontological identity and conceptual plurality?

Does the Apex analogy accurately model the metaphysical relation between the divine essence and attributes, or do disanalogies between a coded integer and a metaphysically simple substance weaken the objection's extension to the divine case?

Is sense-based individuation metaphysically sufficient for genuine theological plurality, or does it reduce divine attributes to mere modes of presentation without distinct causal or explanatory roles?
paper_direction: A paper here would argue that the inference from divine simplicity to the oneness of divine attributes is invalid unless supplemented by a controversial premise that ontological identity precludes any difference in meaning, account, or scope. The case would develop the Apex analogy to demonstrate that strict identity of an underlying ground is compatible with genuine plurality of attributes when they are individuated by sense or functional role, and it would contend that the Ash'arite strategy of distinguishing divine attributes by their distinct accounts is sufficient to block the collapse into a single attribute. The strongest reply to anticipate is that the game analogy trades on merely accidental sameness of numerical value rather than the metaphysical sameness of essence and attribute, or that conceptual distinction without ontological difference cannot yield theologically robust plurality. To succeed, the paper would need to show that sense-based individuation is metaphysically coherent in the divine case and that the critic's demand for ontological differentiation among attributes begs the question against the simplicity theorist's framework.

reasons.coherence: The objection targets c004, which follows trivially from strict identity, when its real target is c003 or c005; the game case shows distinct attributes sharing a value, not identical attributes being many.
reasons.robustness: The equivocation reply is obvious and decisive against the paper as framed, and the plan's charge that the critic begs the question does not answer it, since counting identical items as one is not a contested premise.
reasons.significance: Even if it succeeded, the result restates the well-known move that divine predicates differ in sense but share one referent, and a closely matching paper already exists.
reasons.specificity: There is a stated thesis, a case and a list of what must be shown, but the case is a shallow analogy and the plan does not engage the existing simplicity models it would need to improve on.

assessment.strongest_objection: The objection equivocates on 'attribute'. In the Apex case HP, ATK and SPD are three distinct variables that happen to share a value, so they are not strictly identical. And if divine attributes are strictly identical with one another, as c003 says, then by the logic of identity and counting there is exactly one attribute. c004 is therefore near-analytic, and what remains plural is only predicates or senses. That is the standard Fregean/Thomist reading (Mann, Brower, Aquinas), and it concedes c004 while relocating the dispute to c003 or c005.
assessment.what_it_needs: The paper must drop the claim that c004 is invalid. It should instead argue against c003's step from simplicity to strict identity of properties, or argue that c005's multiplicity worry is satisfied by a plurality of senses or predicates. It must also show what it adds beyond existing Fregean and truthmaker readings of simplicity and the Plantinga–Ghazālī literature the lab flagged as making the same move.
assessment.summary: As framed this would be rejected: it mistakes a familiar sense/reference point for a refutation of an analytic premise, and it would need to be retargeted at c003 or c005 and positioned against the existing literature to be worth writing.

revision.research_question: Once strict identity of each divine attribute with the divine essence is granted, so that the attributes count as one, can a genuine plurality of divine predicates individuated by sense or role answer the multiplicity worry in c005 without reintroducing distinct attributes?
revision.paper_direction: A paper here would argue that the referee is correct that c004 follows from c003 and cannot be rejected as invalid, so the paper drops that claim. It would grant that strict identity of every divine attribute with the divine essence yields a single attribute in the counting sense, and locate the live dispute in c005, the claim that the multiplicity of omnipotence, omniscience, and omnibenevolence is hard to accept. The Apex case is repurposed as a diagnostic rather than a proof. Its stat screen shows three bars, but the designers' three attributes are distinct variables sharing a value, which is exactly the reading the simplicity theorist must reject. The paper would argue that the Apex analogy therefore sharpens the question: whether divine plurality can be located in the plurality of senses, accounts, or predicates that a single attribute supports, rather than in distinct attributes. It would then test that move against the existing Fregean and Thomist readings and the Plantinga and Ghazālī literature the lab flagged. The contribution is confined to showing whether sense-based plurality can do the explanatory work c005 requires, namely that omnipotence and omnibenevolence differ in what they say about God, without ontological difference among attributes, and whether that account is stable once c006's worry about abstract properties is also addressed. The paper claims no novelty for the basic Fregean distinction; its claim is limited to specifying the conditions under which sense-based plurality meets c005.
revision.reply_to_strongest_objection: The paper concedes the equivocation charge. c004 is not an independent target: given c003, identical attributes count as one, so the paper does not argue that c004 is invalid. The Apex case is then used to show what the objection actually turns on. HP, ATK and SPD are distinct variables sharing a value and are therefore not identical, so the game supports plurality only if the divine case is read as distinct items. The paper's reply is a distinction between attributes as items that bear properties and predicates or senses by which one item is presented. It argues that c005's multiplicity worry is answered by plurality of senses or predicates, and it tests whether that answer is adequate. The referee's relocation to c003 or c005 is accepted as the correct site of dispute, and the paper addresses c005 directly.
revision.what_changed: The revision drops the claim that c004 is invalid, concedes that it follows from strict identity, and relocates the paper's thesis to whether sense-based plurality answers the multiplicity objection in c005.

reasons.coherence: The direction abandons the objection to the challenged premise c004 and retargets c005. It describes the Apex attributes as distinct variables, which contradicts the original case where they were explicitly not distinct variables. It also credits Ash'arites with an identity-plus-conceptual-plurality view, but they standardly deny that the attributes are identical with the essence, so the textual reading is unsteady.
reasons.robustness: The obvious referee reply, that this is the familiar Thomist and Fregean answer and has already been done for exactly this debate, is not answered. The plan disclaims novelty for the distinction but names no concrete further condition that would make the paper new.
reasons.significance: Even if it succeeded, the paper would at most restate a known reply to the c005 multiplicity worry, which gives little leverage on the debate.
reasons.specificity: There is a recognisable thesis (sense-plurality answers c005 without reintroducing distinct attributes) and a named set of foils. But the 'conditions' the paper promises are never specified, and the role of the Apex case remains muddled.

assessment.strongest_objection: The paper offers no original contribution. Its core move is the standard reply to Plantinga: the attributes are one in reality and many in sense, concept, or ratio. That reply is found in Aquinas, in Mann and in Stump and Kretzmann, and, in truthmaker form, in Brower. The lab's own literature search classes the closest Plantinga–Ghazālī paper as 'same_move'. Once c004 is conceded, the Apex case does no work: its attributes are distinct variables, not identical ones. What remains is a survey of a well-worked reply without a new condition, argument or case.
assessment.what_it_needs: It must state a specific, defensible condition for when sense-plurality meets c005 that existing accounts (Aquinas's ratio, Brower's truthmaker view, Mann's property-instance view) lack, and defend it against Plantinga's own rejoinder about c006. It should drop the Apex analogy or rebuild it as a genuine identity case, and correct its account of the Ash'arite position.
assessment.summary: A competent reader would see this as a relabelled version of the standard ratio/sense reply to Plantinga, with an analogy that no longer fits and a shaky account of the Ash'arite position, so it is not yet a paper.
